verdict.title: Result of this run
verdict.protected: Voltify warned {{lead}} minutes before the BMS. After the intervention the temperature stopped rising at a peak of {{peak}}°C and then fell; the pack never reached 65°C. With the traditional BMS the pack reached {{bmsPeak}}°C and the bike stopped on the road.
verdict.control: Ordinary hot day: Voltify raised no alert and took no action, and both sides are identical (no false alarm).
verdict.stillTrips: Cutting power 15% alone slowed the temperature rise but the pack still reached 65°C and the BMS cut off ({{delay}} minutes later than with no intervention). Swapping the pack is the decisive step.
verdict.holdsWithoutSwap: Cutting power alone kept the pack below 65°C in this run (peak {{peak}}°C), but it stays hot because it has not been swapped.

notes.title: Read the result with care
notes.severe: This is a deliberately severe scenario (a worst day), not a typical situation. Results over many scenarios and random seeds are in the Evidence tab.
notes.lead: Lead time here is the number measured in this simulation. The 30–45 minute figure is a target to be confirmed in a pilot on real vehicles, not a conclusion of this PoC.
notes.derate: A 15% power cut slows the temperature rise; it is the swap (removing the load) that stops it. For heat from inside the pack (an internal short) cutting load cannot stop the heat: then Voltify's value is early warning and isolating the pack.
notes.assumptions: Swap time is computed from the distance to the nearest station with a cool pack (assumptions: shipper reacts in 30 s, rides at 6 m/s, 90 s to hand over). The simulation does not include the secondary exothermic reactions of lithium-ion cells (real thermal runaway).

healthy.name: Healthy pack, ordinary day
healthy.desc: Control: a normal pack on an ordinary day. The Risk Score must stay at Safe.

overload.name: Overload in the heat
overload.desc: The hero scenario of the BMS vs Voltify screen, but here only observed (no intervention) so you can follow the AI's reasoning step by step.

shortCircuit.name: An internal short developing
shortCircuit.desc: From minute 20 one cell starts to leak charge and gets steadily worse. The AI sees the cell drifting and heat that cannot be explained.

weakCell.name: Weak cell (imbalance)
weakCell.desc: One cell has lost 18% of its capacity and has 1.7 times the resistance. This is a maintenance matter, not an immediate fire risk.

aged.name: Heavily aged pack
aged.desc: SOH around 72% with high internal resistance. The AI estimates ageing from resistance and classifies the pack for routing.

risk.title: Risk Score
risk.learning: The AI is still learning this pack (the first few minutes), so it only uses directly measured quantities.

unexplained_heat.name: Heat the standard model cannot explain
unexplained_heat.hint: Excess heat power over what the current and weather account for. A rising value is an early sign of an internal short or poor cooling.

eta_to_limit.name: Forecast time to the 65°C limit
eta_to_limit.hint: Extrapolated from the present heating trend; the shorter, the more dangerous. A forecast, not a promise.

core_temp.name: Pack core temperature
core_temp.hint: Measured directly; risk starts counting from 52°C.

cell_sag.name: A cell sagging below the group
cell_sag.hint: How far the lowest cell sits below the median, with the current-dependent part removed, expressed as an equivalent % SOC. A leaking or badly unbalanced cell is off at every current.

cell_drift.name: A cell drifting away from the group
cell_drift.hint: A cell that has changed relative to the group over the last ~25 minutes, which catches an internal short while the offset is still small.

weak_cell.name: Weak cell (higher resistance than its neighbours)
weak_cell.hint: A maintenance finding rather than a fire signal, so its weight is capped.

cell_voltage_limit.name: Cell voltage outside its limits
cell_voltage_limit.hint: A cell below 2.8 V or above 4.3 V.

overload_crate.name: Current beyond the safe curve for the temperature
overload_crate.hint: RMS current over the continuous current allowed at the present temperature; above 1 is an overload.

hot_charge.name: Charging while the pack is hot
hot_charge.hint: Charging with the core above 45°C ages the pack faster and adds risk.

low_soh.name: Heavily aged (low SOH)
low_soh.hint: SOH estimated from internal resistance. A weak pack heats more easily, but on its own it is not a fire risk.

trace.title: How it is calculated: {{name}}

formulas.levels: Packs are counted by their current Risk Score: Safe below 25, Watch from 25, Warning from 50, Danger from 75 (with hysteresis so the level does not flicker). Packs the AI is still learning count as Safe until it has enough data.
formulas.meanSoh: Mean SOH estimated from internal resistance (RLS, referred to 25°C) over packs past the learning phase. Packs still learning are left out. This is an estimate on simulated data.
formulas.alerts: The number of times a pack rose to the Warning level (Risk Score of 50 or more) since the simulation started. Each change of level counts once.
formulas.swaps: Packs swapped at a station under the intervention policy: alert, derate by 15% after 10 s, notify the shipper, swap after the shipper's reaction time plus the ride to the station plus 90 s of handling.
formulas.prevented: Incidents prevented = packs a traditional BMS cut off at 65°C in the control fleet (same seed, same scenario, no intervention) that were not cut off in the Voltify fleet. Only what is measured in the simulation is counted.
formulas.savings: Savings = incidents prevented × (pack cost × share of value lost when overheated + cost of one vehicle stopped on the road). The factors are illustrative assumptions, listed below.

trace.placeholder: These are illustrative assumptions so the PoC can run, not real customer figures. A pilot replaces them with real numbers; the ROI screen lets you edit them.
trace.counterfactual: The control fleet runs alongside in the same simulation with no intervention at all, so this number is a direct comparison, not a guess.

soc.title: State of Charge (SOC)
soc.explain: SOC is the energy left compared with full, like the fuel gauge of a vehicle. Voltify estimates the minutes of riding left from recent consumption and sets that beside the distance to the nearest battery-swap station.
soc.idle: The vehicle is almost unloaded, so the remaining riding time cannot be estimated yet.
soc.remaining: About {{minutes}} minutes of riding left at the recent load.
soc.station: Nearest swap station {{id}}: {{distance}} m away, about {{minutes}} minutes of riding.
soc.alertReach: Charge is low for the distance to the station: swap now.
soc.alertSwap: The pack is nearly flat: swap at the nearest station.

health.title: State of Health (SOH)
health.explain: SOH shows how much of its original capacity the pack can still use. Voltify estimates it from internal resistance: the more aged the pack, the higher its resistance. The class puts good packs on long routes and weak ones on short trips or in for service.

route.short: Keep to short trips or send for service.

safety.title: Safety and fire risk
safety.explain: Risk Score (0 to 100) combines the four AI modules: thermal trend, cell voltage, overload and internal resistance. The higher the score, the sooner action is needed. The signals contributing most are listed below.
safety.eta: Forecast to reach 65°C in about {{minutes}} minutes if the load stays the same.

discharge.title: Discharge performance
discharge.explain: The discharge score shows how well the pack delivers power. High resistance turns energy into heat; a weak cell or an imbalance between cells cuts the usable power. Each cause is deducted with a fixed weight (50% resistance, 25% weak cell, 25% imbalance).
discharge.balance: Run a cell-balancing cycle on this pack at its next charge; this is maintenance, not a fire risk.

fleet.title: Whole fleet: distribution of the four vital signs
fleet.dischargeNote: Packs the AI is still learning are left out.

phases.title: Two stages of rollout (Known limits & Roadmap)
phases.one: Stage 1 (pilot): monitoring and alerts only. Voltify notifies the shipper and the fleet manager through an app and does not control the vehicle, so no control access from the vehicle maker is needed.
phases.two: Stage 2: send commands back to the vehicle (for example a 15% discharge-power cut) and to the charging cabinet. This needs a technical agreement with the vehicle maker and the BMS maker. This screen simulates both stages to show the value of acting.

controls.hint: Choose a battery brand to follow the intervention of one pack of that brand. The vehicle uses the same scenario and seed as the BMS-vs-Voltify screen, so the figures on the two screens can be checked against each other.

vehicle.title: A vehicle on the road: from alert to swap
vehicle.intro: A 43°C day, an aged pack, a heavy load and a climb. When the Risk Score reaches the Warning level, Voltify sends a power cut down to the vehicle, tells the shipper to swap at the nearest station that has a cool pack, and records the swap. Every time shown comes from the simulation.

cabinet.title: Charging cabinet: cutting the charge current when the pack is too hot
cabinet.intro: The same pack, seed and fast-charging cabinet standing in the sun, run twice: an ordinary cabinet, and a cabinet where Voltify reduces the charging current along the temperature derating curve. The two runs are identical up to the first command.

kpi.title: The two charges compared
kpi.fade: Capacity fade per cycle (during the charge)

trace.title: How the projected life is calculated
trace.formula: Fade per equivalent cycle = charge share × fade while charging + (1 − charge share) × fade while riding. Cycles to SOH 80% = 20% / fade per cycle. Days = cycles / cycles per day. The fade while charging is measured in the simulation (current-weighted mean); the fade while riding follows the Arrhenius equation at the assumed riding temperature.

cabinet.logTitle: Log of commands sent to the cabinet

notes.title: Worth knowing
notes.scenario: Scenario: a fast-charging (1C) cabinet standing in the sun, 46 to 50°C inside, an aged pack (SOH 78%) put on charge a few degrees hotter than the surroundings. A deliberately harsh case.
notes.tradeoff: Trade-off: keeping the pack inside the derating curve makes the charge take about {{ratio}} times as long as charging at full current.
notes.tradeoffUnknown: Trade-off: one of the two charges did not reach full within the simulation.
notes.projection: The roughly {{gain}}% longer life is a projection from the Arrhenius ageing model with the assumptions above, not a measured result. The target of about 35% longer pack life has to be confirmed in a pilot.
notes.cooling: Cutting the charge current is only one layer of protection; cooling the cabinet and moving charging to cooler hours are further options not simulated in this PoC.
notes.window: Shown up to {{end}} (min:s) of the simulated session, seed {{seed}}.

sources.title: 3 raw data sources
sources.desc: Each maker sends telemetry in its own format: field names, units, the sign of the current, the style of the timestamp and the reporting interval all differ.

adapter.title: Normalising adapter
adapter.desc: Recognises the maker from the shape of the message, converts units and sign, rebuilds each cell. A broken message is refused with a reason and never stops the stream.

schema.title: One common schema (Telemetry)
schema.desc: Everything behind the adapter sees a single shape: pack id, time, every cell voltage, current, temperature, SOC, position.

ai.title: One AI Engine
ai.desc: The same four modules and one Risk Score scale for every maker, so the alerts of different makers can be compared.

hub.scenarioNote: One pack from each of the three makers runs the Overload in the heat scenario (seed 202, 10 simulated minutes); each reports in its own maker's format.

feeds.title: Three raw sources become one schema
feeds.intro: Above: the message exactly as the maker's server sent it. Below: the result after the adapter. The latest message follows the simulation clock.

shape.A: Flat JSON, snake_case field names, each cell voltage in mV, discharge current positive.
shape.B: Nested JSON, camelCase field names, ISO-8601 time, charge current positive (the opposite of the standard convention).
shape.C: A compact positional array tagged C1; sends only the pack voltage and each cell's offset, temperature at 0.5°C resolution.

feeds.raw: Raw message from the maker's server
feeds.none: No message has arrived yet (press Play).

mapping.title: Field map: who sends what, and how it is converted
mapping.intro: Each row is one field of the standard schema. In each maker's cell: where it sits in the message (green), the maker's unit or encoding, and the conversion. Adding a maker means writing one more adapter; the AI does not change.

unified.title: One unified screen
unified.intro: The same table, the same units, for all three makers. Pack voltage is the sum of the cell voltages; cell spread is the highest cell minus the lowest.
unified.chartTitle: Risk Score of the three makers on one scale
unified.chartIntro: The three makers send data at different rates (5, 10 and 15 s) but go through the same AI, so their scores share one scale. Each maker has its own line style and marker.

fidelity.title: What is lost in conversion? Difference from the sensor reading
fidelity.intro: Each format rounds the data in its own way. The table compares the adapter output with the simulator's sensor reading (mean and maximum over the whole session). These are validation figures; the AI never sees the sensor reading.
fidelity.note: Maker C sends coarser data (0.5°C, whole-percent SOC, cells rebuilt from the pack voltage and offsets), so its error is larger; in this scenario the AI still alerts on maker C within a similar time to the other two. The AI uses each message's timestamp and does not assume an even time step.

try.title: Try your own message
try.intro: Pick a sample or edit the JSON on the left. The adapter recognises the maker from the shape of the message and normalises it, or refuses it with a reason and without crashing.

samples.nonNumeric: Broken: text where a number belongs

invalid_json.title: The JSON cannot be read
invalid_json.body: The text is not valid JSON, for example cut off when a connection dropped. This message is skipped and the others are still processed.

unknown_format.title: Unknown format
unknown_format.body: The shape of the message matches no known maker. An adapter would have to be written for this maker.

malformed.title: A field is missing or the wrong type
malformed.body: The maker was recognised, but a field is missing or is not a number.

out_of_range.title: A value outside physical limits
out_of_range.body: A value (for example a temperature) is outside a plausible range, so it is treated as a sensor fault rather than as data.

limits.title: Known limits
limits.fictional: The three makers here are fictional (names with a like suffix); the formats were written from assumed descriptions, not from any maker's real specification.
limits.adapter: With real makers, each one needs its own adapter and an API agreement. The effort for that has not been measured in the PoC.
limits.moat: The competitive value is in the engine shared across makers (the Cross-brand Digital Twin), not in reading one format.

packs.label: Number of packs
packs.why: The packs of the fleet or station network to monitor. The default is an illustrative size.

packCostVnd.label: Price of one pack (VND)
packCostVnd.why: Replacement price of a pack; shares its value with the Overview screen. Replace with the real contract price.

rideTempC.label: Average operating temperature (°C)
rideTempC.why: Mean core temperature of the pack in use; sets how fast it ages (Arrhenius).

efcPerDay.label: Cycles per day
efcPerDay.why: One equivalent full cycle is one full discharge of the rated capacity. Shippers ride many hours a day so they often do more than one; the default is an illustrative assumption.

saasFeeVndPerPackMonth.label: SaaS fee per pack per month (VND)
saasFeeVndPerPackMonth.why: The price is a business choice not yet made; the default is only for trying the calculator.

chargeShare.label: Share of each cycle spent charging
chargeShare.why: The part of each cycle that happens on charge; used for the benefit of charging cooler.

packKwh.label: Capacity of one pack (kWh)
packKwh.why: The simulated 16S5P pack of 21700 cells is about 1.4 kWh.

electricityVndPerKwh.label: Electricity price (VND/kWh)
electricityVndPerKwh.why: The charging station's tariff; an illustrative assumption to be replaced by a real bill.

chargeEfficiency.label: Charging efficiency (grid to pack)
chargeEfficiency.why: The share of the energy drawn from the grid that really reaches the pack; the rest becomes heat in the charger and pack.

incidentsPerThousandPacksYear.label: BMS cut-offs on the road (per 1,000 packs a year)
incidentsPerThousandPacksYear.why: The baseline frequency has no real data behind it; the default is only illustrative and should be replaced by the customer's operating data.

packDamageFraction.label: Share of pack value lost when overheated
packDamageFraction.why: Value lost to faster ageing or write-off when a pack is pushed toward 65°C. Shared with the Overview screen.

strandedCostVnd.label: Cost of one vehicle stopped on the road (VND)
strandedCostVnd.why: Covers late orders, a recovery trip and lost shift time. Shared with the Overview screen.

onboardingVndPerPack.label: One-off onboarding cost per pack (VND)
onboardingVndPerPack.why: Work to integrate the API and set up, paid once. An illustrative assumption.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.intro: The first five fields are the main inputs. Every value can be edited and the results on the right update at once. The defaults are illustrative assumptions only.

cooling.title: Cooler charging
cooling.body: A fast-charging cabinet in the sun: the mean core temperature while charging is {{withCut}}°C when Voltify cuts the charge current, against {{without}}°C without it, a drop of {{drop}}°C.

prevention.title: Incidents prevented
prevention.body: In a simulated fleet of {{packs}} packs run for {{minutes}} minutes, the traditional BMS cut off {{trips}} packs in the control fleet; Voltify prevented {{prevented}} (a rate of {{rate}}%).
prevention.none: In a simulated fleet of {{packs}} packs run for {{minutes}} minutes, the traditional BMS had no pack to cut off, so there is no rate yet.

measured.caveat: The sample is small (a handful of incidents) and the packs in trouble are built into the simulated fleet, so this is a measurement on the simulation, not a rate to expect in the field. It can be edited in the table on the right.

careful.title: Careful
careful.desc: Counts only what the PoC measured

target.title: Target
target.desc: The targets of the brief, to be confirmed in a pilot

levers.intro: Only three quantities differ between the two cases. Each cell says where its value comes from: measured in the simulation, a target of the brief that a pilot must confirm, or typed in by you.

why.electricitySavingPct: The part of the charging electricity bill that is saved.
why.preventionPct: The part of the BMS cut-offs on the road that Voltify prevents.

levers.derived: From a {{drop}}°C cooler charge, through the Arrhenius model

results.title: Results per year
results.intro: The two cases side by side, calculated from the inputs on the left. Click the name of a figure to see its formula and the numbers substituted into it.
results.clickHint: Every figure can be traced: click its name to see the formula, the inputs and the assumptions.

replacement.label: Pack replacement cost saved
replacement.hint: Fewer packs to replace each year when packs last longer, times the price of a pack

life.label: Longer pack life
life.hint: From the life predicted from temperature and cycles (to SOH 80%)

energy.label: Electricity saved
energy.hint: The yearly charging electricity bill times the saved share

incidents.label: Incidents prevented
incidents.hint: BMS cut-offs on the road each year that Voltify prevents

net.label: Net benefit after the SaaS fee
net.hint: Total savings minus the subscription fee

payback.label: Payback time
payback.hint: The one-off onboarding cost divided by the monthly net benefit

values.perFee: benefit is {{ratio}} times the SaaS fee

formulas.replacement: Packs replaced per year = packs × 365 / life (days). Saving = (packs replaced before minus after) × pack price, where life with Voltify = life before × (1 + extension).
formulas.life: Life (days) = (1 minus the end-of-life SOH of 0.8) / fade per cycle / cycles per day. Fade per cycle follows Arrhenius (Ea 20 kJ/mol) at the operating temperature. Life with Voltify = life × (1 + extension).
formulas.energy: Energy per year (kWh) = packs × cycles per day × 365 × kWh per pack / charging efficiency. Bill = kWh × electricity price. Saving = bill × saved share.
formulas.incidents: Incidents per year = packs × rate / 1,000. Prevented = incidents × prevention rate. Value = prevented × (pack price × share of value lost when overheated + cost of one vehicle stopped on the road), the same formula as the KPI on the Overview screen.
formulas.net: Net benefit = pack replacement saving + electricity saving + value of incidents prevented − SaaS fee (packs × fee × 12). The break-even extension is the one at which the net benefit is zero, other quantities held.
formulas.payback: Payback (months) = onboarding cost (packs × cost per pack) / monthly net benefit. There is no payback if the net benefit is not positive.

steps.replacementsBefore: Packs replaced per year, without Voltify
steps.replacementsAfter: Packs replaced per year, with Voltify

steps.incidentSaving: Value of incidents prevented per year

chart.verdict: With the current assumptions, Voltify only has to make packs last about {{pct}}% longer for the benefits to cover the SaaS fee (other quantities as in the Careful case).

limits.title: Known limits
limits.illustrative: The pack price, SaaS fee, electricity price, incident frequency and onboarding cost are illustrative assumptions so the model can run; replace them with the customer's own figures.
limits.target: The targets of about 35% longer pack life and about 20% lower electricity cost are targets to be confirmed in a pilot, not measured results.
limits.measured: The Careful case uses only figures measured in the simulation: the cooler charge in a hot cabinet and the prevention rate on a small simulated fleet. An electricity saving has not been measured, so it is counted as 0.
limits.noPromise: This is a tool for trying numbers, not a promise of revenue or savings.

rules.title: How it is counted: what is an incident, what is normal
rules.intro: An event is something the simulator knows happened: the pack had an internal short, or the traditional BMS had to cut it off because its core reached 65°C. The AI counts as having detected it when its Risk Score ever reached the Warning level (50 points). Two kinds of pack are not clear-cut and are handled by the two choices below, both of which can be changed.
rules.nearMiss: Packs that nearly reached the limit
rules.nearMissHint: The core reached {{temp}}°C or more but the BMS did not cut off and there was no short.
rules.maintenance: The fleet with a weak cell

maintenanceOptions.normal: Count as normal: an alert is a false alarm (default)

rules.maintenanceHint: A weak cell is a maintenance matter, not a fire risk, but the voltage module has trouble telling it from a leaking cell.

headline.recallHint: Of the real events, how many the AI alerted on.
headline.precisionHint: Of the packs the AI alerted on, how many really had an event. It depends on the share of events in the sample.
headline.farHint: Of the normal packs, how many the AI alerted on.
headline.aucHint: The probability that the AI scores an event higher than a normal pack. 1 means perfect separation, 0.5 means chance.
headline.leadHint: From the AI's alert to the traditional BMS cutting off at 65°C. The 30 to 45 minute target has to be confirmed in a pilot.
headline.sample: Counted: {{packs}} packs, of which {{events}} events and {{normals}} normal packs ({{prevalence}}% events). Every rate is true only for this sample and this way of counting.

names.shortNeighbour: Healthy packs next to a shorted one

reasons.baseline: no case of this kind in the sample.
reasons.heatwave43: no case of this kind in the sample.
reasons.agedHigh: no case of this kind in the sample.
reasons.heavyClimb: a very heavy load pushes the current past the safe curve, so the AI flags overload although the pack has no fault.
reasons.cellImbalance: a weak cell skews the voltages like a leaking cell and the voltage module cannot fully tell them apart. A false alarm for fire but right about the need for maintenance.
reasons.severeHeatLoad: the pack got hot but not to 60°C. The AI alerts because the temperature is rising and the load is too heavy; under the strict count it is still a false alarm.
reasons.short_veryMild: a very mild short gives off too little heat to reach the Warning level within the simulated window.
reasons.shortNeighbour: a healthy pack alerted by mistake.

cases.missIntro: Real events the AI never took to the Warning level. Click a case to replay that very pack.
cases.missEmpty: No missed cases in this sample. That does not prove the AI never misses.
cases.falseIntro: Normal packs the AI alerted on. Grouped by cause so the commonest kind of error stands out.
cases.falseEmpty: No false alarms in this sample.

soh.title: SOH module: estimate against the simulator's truth
soh.intro: The AI estimates State of Health (SOH) from internal resistance. Each dot is one pack of the fault-free fleets after 75 minutes; a dot on the dashed line is a perfect estimate.

cols.classes: Put in the right good, fair, weak class

soh.note: Makers that report less often (B every 10 s, C every 15 s) lose the current history between two messages, so their estimate is worse; this is a limit of the data, not of tuning.

real.title: Real data: NASA PCoE, ageing Li-ion cells
real.intro: Four 18650 cells (B0005, B0006, B0007, B0018) were charged and discharged repeatedly at room temperature until they lost 30% of their rated 2 Ah capacity, with impedance (Re + Rct) measured along the way. The true SOH is the measured capacity. The question: does the law of the SOH module (resistance / resistance when new = 1 + γ × (1 − SOH)) hold on these real cells?
real.chartAria: SOH measured from capacity and SOH estimated from resistance, cell {{cell}}
real.eol: End of life of the experiment (1.4 Ah)

cols.module: SOH error with the module's γ (% points)
cols.others: SOH error with γ from the other 3 cells (% points)
cols.baseline: Error if the cell is always taken as new (% points)

real.colsNote: The error is the mean size of the difference between the estimated and the true SOH over the cell's impedance measurements. The module uses γ = {{gamma}}, an assumption of the simulation.
real.findingTitle: Result: the simulation's assumption does not hold on these real cells
real.finding: The resistance of the real cells rises far less than assumed: the γ that fits each cell is only {{gMin}} to {{gMax}}, whereas the module uses {{gamma}}. So with the module's γ the estimated SOH is off by {{mMin}} to {{mMax}} % points, hardly better than taking the cell as new. Calibrating γ on the other 3 cells is not enough either: it is off by {{oMin}} to {{oMax}} % points.
real.consequence: Consequence: the law from resistance to SOH has to be calibrated for each type of pack with pilot data, and cross-checked against a capacity-based estimate. The small errors in the simulated table above only mean something inside the simulation.
real.scope: Scope: this test checks the law from resistance to SOH, not the online RLS estimator (which needs pack telemetry with current steps). The impedance here is measured by EIS whereas Voltify estimates it from telemetry; and a small 18650 cell at room temperature differs from an electric-moped pack.

items.simulated: Except for the SOH test on NASA's real data, every result here is on simulated data. The AI was tuned on the same kind of physics it is evaluated on, so the gap between simulation and reality (the sim-to-real gap) is the biggest unknown; only a pilot with real telemetry can answer it.
items.event: An event here is an internal short or a BMS cut-off at 65°C, not a real fire; the simulation does not reproduce fires. Packs that reached {{temp}}°C without the BMS cutting off are handled separately and can be counted differently.
items.lead: The measured lead time is below the 30 to 45 minute target. The live forecast of the time left to 65°C is usually more optimistic than reality; it is a forecast, not a promise.
items.short: Cutting power by 15% only slows the rise when the heat comes from the load; for an internal short, Voltify's value is early warning and isolation (a swap), not making the temperature stop rising.
items.weakCell: A weak cell and a leaking cell give similar voltage signals, so part of the weak-cell fleet is alerted; that is a false alarm for fire but useful for maintenance.
items.slow: A very mild short (final resistance {{ohm}} ohm, about 9 W) gives off too little heat: many such cases are missed within the 100-minute simulated window.
items.soh: SOH estimation is worse for makers that report sparsely. On NASA's real cells the simulation's law from resistance to SOH did not hold (see the real-data part above), so the module's SOH can only be trusted once it has been calibrated on real data.
items.prevalence: Precision depends on the share of events in the sample; a real fleet may have a very different share, so this figure must not be used to predict precision in the field.

roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.one: Stage 1 (pilot): monitoring and alerts only on real telemetry, used to calibrate the thresholds and to measure the real lead time, precision and recall.
roadmap.two: Stage 2: control back to the vehicle and the charging cabinet (power cut, charge-current cut) once stage 1 shows the alerts are reliable enough.
roadmap.three: Widen the SOH validation to other public datasets (for example CALCE), other cells and packs, then to pilot data; calibrate the law from resistance to SOH for each type of pack.

uvp.label: Unique value proposition (UVP)
uvp.statement: Voltify warns early of fire risk and extends battery life for commercial electric mopeds, with cloud software alone, for every battery maker on one screen.

proactive.title: Proactive prediction
proactive.body: A warning tens of minutes ahead (the figure measured on the Evidence screen) instead of waiting for the BMS to cut off passively at 65°C.

saas.title: Pure SaaS
saas.body: Uses the BMS and the GPS/4G module already in the pack, so no new hardware.

agnostic.title: Maker-independent
agnostic.body: Normalises many formats into one Digital Twin and one Risk Score scale, for delivery mopeds and battery-swap stations.

problem.title: The problem
problem.intro: Urban heat of 40 to 43°C (road surface up to about 55°C) together with how hard shippers work the pack (10 to 12 hours a day, heavy continuous current) pushes lithium-ion packs to their limits.

items.fire: Sudden fire: a traditional BMS only cuts off passively once a limit has been reached.
items.aging: Hidden ageing about 30 to 40% faster than normal (per the brief); a company cannot watch each pack and has to replace packs early.
items.downtime: Operational breakdown: a vehicle that dies on the road delays orders.

solution.title: The solution
solution.intro: SaaS running entirely in the cloud. Telemetry (about every 5 seconds) goes from the pack through the vehicle maker's server and over an API to Voltify.

items.cloud: Uses the BMS and the GPS/4G module already in the pack: no extra hardware.
items.twin: Builds a Digital Twin of each pack from four measurements: every cell voltage, charge and discharge current, internal temperature and internal resistance.
items.cross: Normalises many makers into one schema and one operations screen (Cross-brand Hub).
items.assets: Optimises the battery asset: good packs on long routes, weak packs on short trips or in for service.

hints.startWarmC: A pack just off a hot charging cabinet is usually a few degrees warmer than the air.
hints.payloadKg: A heavy load means more current and so more heat.
hints.climbDutyPct: The part of the ride spent on slopes.
hints.sohPct: The more aged the pack, the higher its resistance and the more heat it makes.

notes.title: Worth knowing in the Sandbox
notes.same: Both sides use the same seed and scenario; every difference is due to Voltify's commands (power cut, swap), not to chance.
notes.short: With an internal short the heat comes from the short itself, so cutting power only slows it; the swap is what removes the load. A mild short may go unseen in a short run (see the Evidence screen).
notes.limits: This is a simulation with assumed parameters, not a prediction for any one vehicle.

intro.title: A {{minutes}}-minute automatic demo
intro.body: It walks through four screens: the fleet overview, the traditional BMS vs Voltify, the intervention mechanism and the ROI, each with captions. Every number in the captions comes from the simulation itself. Press Esc or Exit to stop at any time.
intro.sandbox: Or try it yourself in the Sandbox
intro.repeatable: The demo is repeatable: the fleet uses seed 2026 and the BMS-vs-Voltify case uses seed 202, so every run tells the same story. You can pause, jump to another step, or click around the screens yourself (the demo then pauses and waits for you).

fleet.name: Fleet overview
fleet.what: A map of 300 packs by risk level, with KPIs you can trace.

bms.name: Traditional BMS vs Voltify
bms.what: One bad day, two outcomes: the BMS cuts off at 65°C, Voltify warns early.

intervention.name: Intervention mechanism
intervention.what: The shipper's phone, the command log and the pack swap.

roi.name: ROI and Impact
roi.what: Net benefit, payback and the life extension needed to break even.

fleet.b1: This is a simulated fleet of 300 packs in Ho Chi Minh City and Hanoi, one point per pack. Shape and colour show the risk level: Safe, Watch, Warning, Danger.
fleet.b2: Voltify watches every pack continuously. The pack with the highest Risk Score has just been selected: its readings and status are on the right.
fleet.b3: Every number here can be traced: click the Incidents prevented KPI to see the formula and the control fleet with no intervention.

bms.b1: The same 43°C day, an aged pack, a heavy load, a climb. The two sides are identical; the only difference is that the right side has Voltify.
bms.b2: Voltify alerts at {{alert}} and cuts power by {{derate}}%. The traditional BMS does nothing yet because the core has not reached 65°C.
bms.b3: The BMS cuts off at {{trip}} when the core reaches 65°C: the vehicle dies on the road. Voltify warned {{lead}} minutes earlier and the peak was only {{peak}}°C, against {{bmsPeak}}°C with the traditional BMS.

intervention.b1: When the Risk Score reaches the Warning level, the platform sends a {{derate}}% power cut down to the vehicle and tells the shipper.
intervention.b2: The shipper's phone gets a notification: swap at station {{station}}, {{distance}} m away, a cool pack already held. The map is the straight line the simulation assumes.
intervention.b3: The pack is swapped by {{swap}}; the hot pack stays at the station to cool. The command log shows simulated example formats. Stage 1 only alerts; commands down to the vehicle are stage 2.

roi.b1: The ROI calculator: the number of packs, pack price, operating temperature, cycles per day and SaaS fee are all editable. The defaults ({{packs}} packs, a fee of {{fee}} VND per pack per month) are only illustrative assumptions.
roi.b2: The Careful case uses only what the simulation measured: a net benefit of about {{careful}} a year, paid back in {{payback}} months. Packs only need to last about {{breakEven}}% longer for the benefits to cover the SaaS fee.
roi.b3: The Target case (35% longer life, 20% less electricity) gives about {{target}} a year, but that is a target a pilot has to confirm, not a measured result.

end.title: End of the demo
end.body: You have just seen the fleet, the traditional BMS vs Voltify case, the intervention mechanism and the ROI. The evidence and the limits are on the screens below.

limits.simulated: All data is simulated; there is no real battery data yet.
limits.targets: The targets of 30 to 45 minutes of lead time, 35% longer life and 20% less electricity need a pilot to confirm; the measured figures are lower or not yet available.
limits.phases: Stage 1 only monitors and alerts; control back to the vehicle is stage 2.
